symbols.note: Defined in docstring as two-stage: graceful then tree_kill. Not actual code.

claims.text: Popen.send_signal(signal.SIGINT) does not cancel a tree on win32: it is delivered (via the CRT console machinery) to the immediate child only, so grandchildren survive and keep writing files after the caller believes the attempt was cancelled.
claims.why: This claim describes behavior of Popen.send_signal, which is not implemented in this chunk. The claim is about external library behavior, not code present.

claims.text: The cancellation ladder here has two verified stages: 1. graceful -- ask the whole process group to stop. win32: GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent(CTRL_BREAK_EVENT, pgid); posix: killpg(pgid, SIGINT). 2. tree_kill -- if anything is still alive after the grace window, destroy the container. win32: TerminateJobObject; posix: killpg(SIGKILL).
claims.why: The claim describes stages that are not implemented in this chunk. The constants and structures are defined, but the actual logic for graceful and tree_kill is absent.

claims.text: On win32 containment is a Job Object carrying JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE.
claims.why: The constant _JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE is defined at line 72, confirming the claim about the flag.

claims.text: The child is created *suspended* and resumed only after AssignProcessToJobObject succeeded, so there is no window in which the child can spawn a grandchild outside the job.
claims.why: The claim refers to process creation and job assignment logic, which is not present in this chunk. The constant CREATE_SUSPENDED is defined, but no code uses it yet.

claims.text: If the job cannot be created, configured, or assigned, spawning fails closed (CancellationUnavailable) rather than handing back a process whose tree we could not later kill.
claims.why: The exception CancellationUnavailable is defined, but the logic to raise it on job creation failure is not in this chunk.
The code uses ctypes (imported at line 28) and does not import pywin32, confirming the claim.

claims.text: Fail-closed: better to refuse the launch than to run work we cannot cancel.
claims.why: This is a design claim about the exception CancellationUnavailable; the behavior is not demonstrated in this chunk.

claims.text: Which rung of the ladder actually stopped the tree.
claims.why: The CancelResult docstring describes the stage field, but the ladder logic is not present in this chunk.

observations.what: Module docstring describes a two-stage cancellation ladder (graceful then tree_kill) but no implementation of either stage is present in this chunk. Only constants and structures are defined.
Windows-specific constants and structures are defined inside an if _IS_WINDOWS block, but the block is incomplete; it ends mid-structure definition (line 96).
The public API symbols listed in __all__ (e.g., ManagedProcess, select_backend, cancel_all_managed) are not defined in this chunk; they are only referenced as strings.
The module imports weakref, Path, Any, Mapping, Sequence, threading, time, but none are used in this chunk.
